maria: quick perf dump from yesterday's canary run — noticed a bunch of OOMs + kernel fallbacks on long sequences. paste below for visibility.

maria: ```
Perf summary (canary-2026-03-17):
- total requests: 120k
- avg gen latency: 78ms (p99 430ms)
- kernel selection: flash_attn: 61%, f32_fallback: 39%
- KV prefix cache peak: 420GB across 4 hosts
- OOMs: 15 (hosts h12/h14/h17) during concurrent 512/1024 seq requests
Root cause signal: many fallbacks because allocated workspace < requested workspace (ws < ~2.5GB) and allocator fragmentation.
Top noisy path: long-seq batching + aggressive prefetch touched many cold shards.
```

alex: can you paste the shard heatmap + current TTL/shard_size?

maria: here's the heatmap (accesses per shard last 6h) and current config:

maria: ```
Shard heatmap (hot=H warm=W cold=C):
[h1 H H H H W W C C C]
[h2 H H W W C C C C C C]
[h3 H W W C C C C C C C]  (most activity concentrated in first 3 shards)

Current prefixcache config:
- shard_size: 128MB
- shards_per_host: 512
- ttl: 300s
- prefetch_policy: eager
- prefetch_window: 256 tokens
- workspace_pool_per_gpu: 8GB
- slab_size: 16MB
```

sam: quick thoughts:
- hot/cold split looks promising. move to tiered TTL (hot=30s, warm=120s, cold=600s) and smaller cold shard residency to free memory.
- increase buffer reuse: grow per-gpu workspace_pool to 12GB but reduce slab granularity to 8MB to reduce fragmentation.
- batching heuristic: prefer kernel A (flash_attn) only if estimated_ws <= pool_free - safety_margin; otherwise try quantized kernel B before f32 fallback.

maria: ran a sim locally with those tweaks:

maria: ```
Sim results (synthetic 24h replay):
- avg latency: 82ms (+4ms)
- p99: 480ms (+50ms)
- KV mem peak: 344GB (-18%)
- cache hit-rate: 86% (was 90%) -> -4% absolute
- OOMs: 1 (was 15)
Notes: tail latency regressed slightly due to extra quantized fallbacks, but stable (fewer hard OOMs).
```

alex: tradeoffs look fine for canary. We care more about stability than 4% hit-rate. Can we do hybrid eviction: age + access_count so hot shards survive short TTL?

sam: yeah — implement eviction priority = last_access_time * alpha + access_count * beta. alpha=0.6 beta=0.4 in sim. kept hot shards pinned.

jon: question on kernel gating: currently we flip to fallback as soon as alloc fails. Could we gate by "expected_seq > seq_threshold" and also try quantized path first so we don't pay full f32 cost? Also add a fast-path reservation: small pinned workspace for long requests to avoid mid-request failure.

maria: good call. I prototyped a 64MB emergency reservation pool per-GPU for long requests; prevents the common mid-request OOM.

maria: proposed config (canary):

maria: ```yaml
prefixcache:
  tiers:
    - name: hot
      ttl: 30s
      shard_size: 64MB
      max_pinned: 64
    - name: warm
      ttl: 120s
      shard_size: 128MB
    - name: cold
      ttl: 600s
      shard_size: 256MB
allocator:
  workspace_pool_per_gpu: 12GB
  emergency_reservation: 64MB
  slab_size: 8MB
kernel_selection:
  seq_threshold: 384
  prefer_quantized_before_f32: true
  safety_margin: 200MB
eviction:
  policy: age_access
  alpha: 0.6
  beta: 0.4
```

leo: @infra-bot can we roll that config to `canary` env? i'll run a 48h replay afterwards.

infra-bot: Started deployment "prefetch-config-206450" to env=canary. rolling out to 4 hosts. logs: https://deploys.internal/r/206450

infra-bot: Deployment progress: 2/4 hosts updated, no crash, staged health checks OK.

maria: action items:
- leo to run 48h replay + real traffic canary (assign)
- sam to add quantized kernel path and gating logic (sam)
- jon to add emergency reservation metric + alert (oom_rate > 0.5/hr)
- alex to monitor cache hit-rate delta and model quality signals for 48h

maria: thanks all — goal: drop OOMs to 0 on canary without >10% hit-rate loss and keep p99 within +100ms. will follow up with results in this thread. :thumbsup:
